title: Turnstile ’96: I built a football management game with Codex + Claude Code, and the process was pretty chaotic
author: hecticmike-fc
selftext:
I've been working on a football management game called Turnstile '96, and I've finally released the first public version just a few days ago.

It's a  free Windows game inspired by the football managers I grew up playing in the late 90s/early 2000s. You manage the squad, transfers, tactics, finances, stadium and facilities and work your way through multiple seasons. At surface, it was made to look quite linear, but it is really not (there is player and club development, tactical familiarity, and do much more that was added in in a discreet way by design).

I used Codex and Claude Code quite heavily throughout development.

I wish I could say I had a clever workflow where Claude did one thing and Codex did another, but I really didn't. I moved between them depending on what I was working on, which one was giving me better results at the time, or simply because I got stuck and wanted another approach.

Most of the process was something like:

have an idea > get it implemented > play it > realise it isn't quite what I meant > explain why > change it > play it again.

And that repeated a lot.

The coding itself stopped becoming a barrier, but I found that the difficult part moved somewhere else. Things like deciding how player attributes should affect different positions, how quickly players should develop, whether transfers were too easy, whether the finances worked (it was so hard to get the right balance as I didn't want to create a path for you to build the best team in the world in 5 seasons, but I also didn't was to smash your dreams if you were doing a great job), or whether the game was actually fun still required a lot of judgement and testing.

There were also plenty of cases where the AI produced something that technically worked perfectly but was completely wrong for the game I was trying to make.

So AI did a huge amount of the implementation, but the concept, mechanics, balancing, visual direction and decisions about what the game should actually be came from me. I am 100% sure that I couldn't have built something of this size on my own otherwise.

The game now has 45 playable divisions across 30 countries, player development, transfers, live matches, promotion/relegation, cups, club finances, stadium and facility development and a proper multi-season career (potentially endless).

This is what it eventually became:

[https://hecticmike.itch.io/turnstile96](https://hecticmike.itch.io/turnstile96)

I'm curious whether other people using Codex and Claude Code together have a clear way of deciding which one to use for what, because I definitely didn't... and wish I had.
